Senses.Explanation: A title-of-honor string invoking all the thus-come ones of past, present, and future as one body, proclaimed in verse and hall address across the corpus. Hongzhi Zhengjue tells the assembly that with neither is nor is-not, neither joined nor parted, the thus-come ones of the three times together proclaim this very meaning; Zhongfeng Mingben opens his instruction with the teaching's word that they all appeared in the world for the one great matter; and Liao'an Qingyu works it into verse for a visiting guest — one tongue for all the three times, nothing to say in the whole canon. Gulin Qingmao's matched reply verse sings one nature for the three times with nothing left over for the stirring and wriggling; Weilin Daopei, consecrating the three-times statues, points out the one truth-body whose lit radiance shows its bearing; Konggu Daocheng tells the hall that apart from empty and not-empty they are all one alike; Yezhu Fuhui tells the layman straight that the ten kinds of beings are a dream and the three-times thus-come ones its dreamers; and Yunwai Xingze, at the frost-wood hall, has the original face with nowhere to hide and the three-times thus-come ones' mouths gone dry.
